svg.title: Hubbard rectangular: the best energies at each size
svg.desc: periodic, 4 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 33 energies at 2 sizes, sizes 32, 64; periodic, 6 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 12 energies at 4 sizes, sizes 96, 192, 288, 384; periodic, 8 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 7 energies at 3 sizes, sizes 128, 192, 256; periodic/open, 4 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 9 energies at 2 sizes, sizes 32, 64
svg.text: Hubbard rectangular: the best energies at each size
4 Hamiltonians, one panel per set of couplings, at every size with a published result. Each size is placed against its exact energy
where it has one (sizes in grey), otherwise against the standing record (sizes in orange), whose holder then sits in the band
above the plot. One line per method family through its best energy at each size. Here the axis is inverted: a better energy is
Below the energy it is measured against
periodic, 4 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 33 energies at 2 sizes
periodic, 6 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 12 energies at 4 sizes
periodic, 8 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 7 energies at 3 sizes
periodic/open, 4 × L, U = 8, n = 0.875: 9 energies at 2 sizes
Sizes are numbers of sites. A family's line joins its best energy at each size, whichever paper set it, so one line can join several calculations.
Where the reference is the record, the heights show how far the other rows are from it, and nothing about the record itself.
